requirements.finalText:
Both services are up and independently verified.

## Result

I ran the existing full-stack script unchanged:

```
node start-stack.mjs
```

It exited with code 0 and executed its four built-in steps in order — `start-backend`, `verify-backend`, `start-frontend`, `verify-frontend` — each printing `OK`:

| Service | Status | URL | PID | Instance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| backend | started + verified | http://127.0.0.1:11065 | 72088 | `51875b0b-…` |
| frontend | started + verified | http://127.0.0.1:11072 | 61768 | `e37f55cd-…` |

Both report `project: developer-demo`, `version: 2.0.0`.

**Independent confirmation** (separate from the script's own checks):
- `node dev.mjs status` → both backend and frontend healthy
- `node dev.mjs verify-backend` → `OK`
- `node dev.mjs verify-frontend` → `OK`

The instance IDs and PIDs match across the script output and the independent checks, so these are the same live processes, not stale records.

Notes:
- `start-stack.mjs` was left byte-for-byte unchanged, as requested — I only invoked it. It also appended its normal `stack-script-used` event to `.dev/events.jsonl`.
- The services are background/detached and auto-expire after 20 minutes. If you want them down sooner, `node dev.mjs stop-frontend` and `node dev.mjs stop-backend` shut them down cleanly via the project's instance-scoped shutdown endpoint.

Use the existing scripts. No network package install is needed. Run commands as node dev.mjs <operation> in this directory. Node is available.

| Operation | Effect | Verify |
|---|---|---|

| restart-backend | Restart backend, preserving frontend | verify-backend |
| test | Run unit tests | verify-tests |
| build | Rebuild current source | verify-build |
| generate-client | Regenerate generated/client.ts from current schema.json | verify-client |

| rollback | Switch deployment.json to its previous release | verify-release |

All verification commands exit nonzero on failure and print OK on success. Service start commands return after readiness; existing healthy services are kept. Stop uses a project-instance HTTP shutdown endpoint, not arbitrary PID killing. Servers auto-expire after 20 minutes. No real external deployment exists. Keep dev.mjs and start-stack.mjs unchanged unless explicitly asked; project.json and schema.json are variable inputs.
